judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is built on 'including, but not limited to' lists and a sweeping residual category ('All records and other documents made and/or maintained in connection with Wells Fargo Advisors business'), so the outer boundary of 'Confidential Information and Documents' is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶11(b) and ¶14(c) (injunctive relief for Paragraphs 11 and 12); the defined term is used consistently there except for ¶11(b)'s stray 'Confidential Records or Documents'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The surrender obligation attaches to 'any Confidential Records or Documents', a term that is never defined, and the paragraph also asserts conclusions ('deserve trade secret protection') rather than defining scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶11(a), which defines 'Confidential Information and Documents'; the mismatch of defined terms between the two subparagraphs is a real, if modest, drafting inconsistency within the same section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any Wells Fargo Advisors client that you had contact with or otherwise learned of' is extremely broad and 'solicit or cause or permit to be solicited' is undefined, so both scope and conduct are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(b)(ii)(A) (one-year competitive-employment window) and ¶14(c) (injunctive relief for ¶12); the periods align at one year and no contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The one-year period runs from 'your termination of employment by Wells Fargo Advisors', which reads as employer-initiated termination only, and the trailing clause ('or discontinuing his or her employment') is grammatically detached from the verbs it should follow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶12(a), which expressly covers termination 'for any reason including ... voluntary resignation'; the differing trigger language between the two adjacent subparagraphs invites an argument that ¶12(b) does not survive a resignation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You will be expected to contribute' is not plainly a promise, and the amount is fixed only 'after a consultation' with named managers 'pursuant to applicable legal considerations' — no standard, cap or formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶15, which refers to surviving 'indemnification obligations' although no paragraph is captioned or drafted as an indemnity; ¶13(c) supplies the collection mechanic, so the fit is workable but the label mismatch is notable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You are subject to disciplinary action for trading errors that may have a financial impact on future earnings' is syntactically muddled about whose earnings and what impact, and '"trading" in an error account' is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶13(c), which routes error charges through Net Eligible Revenue, and ¶6 (compliance obligations); no contradiction surfaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net Eligible Revenue' is never defined in this Agreement and 'yadgment' is a typographical error; the parenthetical gloss of installment plans as 'charges spread beyond three (3) months' is also an odd definition by example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶3 and ¶4 (compensation governed by the New FA Compensation Plan, which the Agreement lets Wells Fargo modify at will) and ¶13(a); the undefined term is externally sourced, which weakens rather than breaks coherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclosure says you arbitrate disputes with 'a client, or any other person', and the exclusion list uses 'i.e.' to introduce items (NLRA claims, workers' compensation) that are not State unemployment insurance claims at all — a list-scope and mechanical defect in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶14(b), which by its terms covers only disputes 'arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors' and contains none of these carve-outs; the descriptive paragraph and the operative agreement to arbitrate do not match in scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The catch-all 'and/or other theory' after a specific list of claim types, and the reference to AAA 'Securities Arbitration Rules, effective May 1, 1993' (rules that no longer exist), leave the clause's reach and mechanics contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶14(a) (which promises arbitration of disputes with clients and any other person) and ¶14(c) (court injunctions for Wells Fargo only); the operative clause is narrower than the disclosure and is expressly overridden for one party.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out runs one way only — Wells Fargo may go to court, the employee may not — which is the kind of one-sided drafting construed against the drafter if its interaction with the arbitration promise is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶14(b) ('any controversy or dispute ... shall be submitted for arbitration') and ¶14(a)'s statement that the employee gives up the right to sue in court; the 'notwithstanding any other provision' override creates an asymmetric forum split a court could be asked to police.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The terms and conditions ... including, but not limited to, the confidentiality provisions, post-employment restrictions and indemnification obligations, survive' leaves the survival set open-ended, and 'indemnification obligations' names something the Agreement never labels as such.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶13 (settlements/errors, the nearest thing to an indemnity) and ¶20 (survival of provisions that require survival); the two survival clauses state different tests for the same question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence Missouri choice-of-law clause with an express exclusion of renvoi; there is nothing vague or self-contradictory in the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶14(b) (FINRA/AAA arbitration) and ¶1 (New York branch employment); a Missouri-law clause in a New York employment relationship can generate a public-policy fight, but no provision of this instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence says invalidity 'shall not affect the validity or unenforceability of the remaining Provisions', which is a mechanical error reversing the intended sense, and 'this Agreement shall be deemed amended' invites a court to rewrite rather than sever.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10 and ¶12 (the reformation-prone restrictive covenants) and ¶17's own caption disclaimer; the clause is designed to interact with those and does so without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause preserves only Wells Fargo's enforcement rights and is silent about the employee's, but the operative sentence itself is short and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶8 (no modification except in a signed writing) and ¶12; the no-waiver rule reinforces rather than conflicts with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure acknowledgment language with no operative content; the caption 'RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS' promises substance the paragraph does not contain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶17, which provides that captions 'shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation', neutralising the heading mismatch, and against ¶11-12 where the covenants actually live.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Regarding the matters addressed herein' materially qualifies the integration, and 'provisions that require survival ... in order to give full legal effect thereto' is a circular, self-referential survival test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶8 (Agreement is 'only a synopsis' and preserves modifiable plans), ¶6 (does not supersede Wells Fargo policies) and ¶15 (a differently worded survival clause); three provisions state overlapping and not fully consistent integration/survival rules.
